concept.name: Trading routine
concept.definition: The fixed daily and weekly structure around trading - pre-market preparation, defined session behaviors, post-market review - that standardizes decision quality and conserves willpower. Routines externalize discipline into schedule and environment instead of relying on in-the-moment self-control.
concept.intuition: You cannot will yourself into consistency every day; you build a routine so the consistent behavior happens by default.
concept.mechanics: Typical elements: pre-market plan (levels, catalysts, scenarios), warm-up and state check, session rules (trading windows, breaks, loss limits), a shutdown ritual, daily review, and sleep and exercise management. Trading-psychology work such as Steenbarger's emphasizes structured practice and self-coaching routines as the mechanism of trader development.
concept.failure_modes: Routines decay under travel, stress, or overconfidence after good stretches, usually starting with skipped preparation. An overly rigid routine also breaks when market conditions shift the session structure, as on event days.
concept.misconceptions: A routine is not superstition or comfort ritual; its components exist to control preparation quality, arousal, and exposure. Watching screens longer is not a routine - it is often the absence of one.
concept.example: A trader's day: 7:00 review of overnight markets and scenarios, 9:20 checklist and state check, trade only 9:30-11:00, hard daily stop at -2R, journal and review by 16:30 - the same sequence every session.

citations.source: Brett N. Steenbarger, The Psychology of Trading: Tools and Techniques for Minding the Markets (Wiley, 2003) - publisher page
